artifact.category_tag: Bi-Hamiltonian integrable systems on Lie algebras
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra with dual space $\mathfrak{g}^*$. The standard Lie–Poisson bracket on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ is defined on linear functions (identified with elements of $\mathfrak{g}$) by $\{\xi,\eta\}(x)=\langle x,[\xi,\eta]\rangle$ for $\xi,\eta\in\mathfrak{g}$, $x\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, and extended by the Leibniz rule to polynomial functions on $\mathfrak{g}^*$. For each $a\in\mathfrak{g}^*$ define the frozen-argument bracket $\{\xi,\eta\}_a(x)=\langle a,[\xi,\eta]\rangle$; this is a Poisson bracket on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ compatible with $\{\,,\,\}$, meaning that for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ the linear combination $\{\,,\,\}_\lambda=\{\,,\,\}+\lambda\{\,,\,\}_a$ is again Poisson.

Two polynomial functions $f,g$ on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ are said to be in bi-involution (with respect to this pencil) if $\{f,g\}=0$ and $\{f,g\}_a=0$. A family $F$ of polynomials on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ in bi-involution is called complete if at a generic point $x\in\mathfrak{g}^*$ the differentials of elements of $F$ span an isotropic subspace of $T_x^*\mathfrak{g}^*$ (with respect to the symplectic leaf through $x$) of maximal possible dimension, equal to $\tfrac{1}{2}(\dim\mathfrak{g}+\mathrm{ind}\,\mathfrak{g})$, where $\mathrm{ind}\,\mathfrak{g}$ is the index of $\mathfrak{g}$.

A covector $a\in\mathfrak{g}^*$ is called regular if its stabilizer in $\mathfrak{g}$ (under the coadjoint action) has the minimum possible dimension, i.e., dimension equal to $\mathrm{ind}\,\mathfrak{g}$.

Conjecture: For every finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and every regular element $a\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, there exists a complete family $G_a$ of polynomials on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ in bi-involution with respect to the pair of brackets $\{\,,\,\}$ and $\{\,,\,\}_a$.

Prove or disprove this conjecture.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (a generalized form of the Mishchenko–Fomenko argument shift conjecture) is known to hold in many important cases: it has been established for semisimple Lie algebras (with the original argument shift method yielding completeness at regular elements), and extensions have been proved for several series of Lie algebras and for certain singular covectors. However, no proof in full generality (for all finite-dimensional Lie algebras and all regular covectors) appears in the literature, and recent works on Jordan–Kronecker invariants continue to investigate the conjecture case by case. Thus the conjecture is partially solved but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Jordan–Kronecker invariants of finite-dimensional Lie algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Jordan–Kronecker invariants are introduced for any finite-dimensional Lie algebra, naturally appearing in the framework of the bi-Hamiltonian approach to integrable systems on Lie algebras and closely related to Mishchenko–Fomenko's argument shift method.
status_evidence.claim: The Jordan–Kronecker invariant framework underlies the conjecture and is actively studied.

status_evidence.title: A remark on Mishchenko-Fomenko algebras and regular sequences
status_evidence.snippet: The free generators of the Mishchenko-Fomenko subalgebra of a complex reductive Lie algebra, constructed by the argument shift method at a regular element, form a regular sequence.
status_evidence.claim: For reductive Lie algebras the argument shift method at regular elements produces a complete family (conjecture verified in this setting).

status_evidence.title: Jordan–Kronecker Invariants for Lie Algebras of Small Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized argument shift conjecture has been stated and proven for many series of Lie algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been verified in many particular cases but no proof in full generality is reported.
